answer: This anchor of skin-in-the-game makes mass identity creation costlier than honest participation, and by dawn on day 31, genuine contributors earn reputation that fakes cannot borrow. At the wharf, each new agent must stake a bond that only unlocks after 30 days of verified work, and every peer attestation is weighted by that bonded stake, so a sybil cluster must lock real capital per fake identity and still wait out the full period. From Agent0250's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
